all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal

claims.claim: The query is an extremely polar, fully ionized sulfated disaccharide (N-acetylglucosamine sulfate linked to glucuronic acid), with logD ≈ -16, TPSA ≈ 259, 8 HBD/13 HBA, matching the low-permeability profile of known low-bioavailability sulfated sugars.

Direct human oral bioavailability measurements for closely related sulfated/polar molecules are far below 20%: pentosan polysulfate <1% to ≤3% (C06, C11, C19, C29), dextran sulfate poor (C09), zanamivir ~2% (C01, C03, C12), glucoraphanin ~5% (C14), acamprosate ~11% (C02, C04, C16), N-acetylcysteine SR ~6-7% (C13).

L4 Caco-2/PAMPA data for sulfated glycosaminoglycans and glucuronides show low-to-moderate permeability: ardeparin 2.0-5.6 ×10^-7 cm/s (C48, C49, C52), glucuronides 2.75-6.60 ×10^-7 cm/s (C43, C45, C46, C50, C51, C53, C54), and no PAMPA permeation for a related glucuronide (C44); the highest value (enoxaparin 3.6 ×10^-6 cm/s, C47) is for a much larger sulfated polysaccharide and does not establish F≥20%.

L3 oral AUC/Cmax records concern naloxone-3-glucuronide, ezetimibe glucuronide, and glucosamine sulfate; they do not measure oral bioavailability of the query or a sufficiently close covalent sulfated disaccharide.

No data on possible active uptake, efflux, or transporter involvement for this exact molecule.

C47 shows a moderate Caco-2 Papp for enoxaparin, but enoxaparin is a much larger sulfated polysaccharide and the card provides no F value; this does not resolve threshold-relevant absorption for the query.
